chapter_title: Concerning the Fourteen Vehicles that Jesus has boarded.
chapter_note: Core material is concentrated in ¶3–8: a numbered, systematic listing of the ten cosmological vehicles (ships/elements/summons-obedience) in an impersonal expository mode. ¶1 is hagiographic frame. ¶9 is a classic editorial seam extending the numbered list into institutional categories (holy church, brothers/sisters, catechumens) and is therefore wholly pastoral. ¶2 and ¶10 present a Christianized/kerygmatic overlay voice (incarnation/manifested in flesh, Father-sending, blessing beatitude) that likely entered with later redaction; the chapter-level fatigue signal aligns with the institutional graft in the second half.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic introduction (“Once again… speaks… to the congregation”) typical of the Kephalaia compilation frame; no teaching content.

Sets the scene with a Christianized descent/mission statement (“came to these worlds… unveiled the greatness”) and a christological title; functions as narrative/kerygmatic preface rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The first vehicle is the light ship, since he received instructions from the Ambassador there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins a numbered cosmological list; uses internal Manichaean hierarchy (“Ambassador”) and vehicle-station logic—hallmark of the systematic teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.37⟩ The second carriage is the ship of the First Man, since his dwelling is established there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered vehicle series with a named cosmic being (First Man) in explanatory, non-citational voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man, since he shone forth there. He came below, he appeared in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the systematic vehicle list; cosmological entities (“Pillar of Glory,” “Perfect Man”) and functional explanation. The descent phrasing remains integrated into the cosmological scheme, not a Gospel citation.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is the summons that he clothed upon his body. The fifth is the obedience that he swathed upon the summons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Abstract redemptive mechanics (Summons/Obedience) expressed as structured items within the numbered sequence—classic core soteriological-cosmological pairing.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth is the living air, and since he assumed it too, he received anointment there. The seventh is the living wind that blows. The eighth is the light that illuminates. The ninth is the living water. The tenth is the living fire that is above them all.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold elemental/living set embedded in the numbered vehicle list; impersonal cataloguing with brief functional glosses—strong core signature.

paragraphs.core_text: He was journeying in these ten carriages among all the orders and all the [...], those above and those below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative closure of the ‘ten vehicles’ sequence, describing cosmic scope (“orders… above and below”); remains within the impersonal teaching register.

Editorial seam flagged: extends the enumerative pattern into institutional categories (“holy church,” “holy brothers,” “pure sisters,” “catechumens”). Entire paragraph is an editorial graft, not mixed.

Redactional theological/praise conclusion: computes 10+4=14, then shifts to kerygmatic salvation language (“Father who sent him,” blessing/beatitude, redeemed vs. strangers). Functions as closing exhortation rather than core structural exposition.
